structure.addressable_unit: A functional prosthetic limb device (lower- or upper-limb prosthesis) supplied or fitted within a year in Germany to a person with major limb loss/absence who is clinically a prosthesis candidate at a qualifying mobility grade and whose device is a reimbursable item listed in the Hilfsmittelverzeichnis.

anchor_type.justification: The market is driven by per-year device fittings and renewals (each supplied prosthesis is a billable provision event), not by a static count of people, so it descends from a count of provision-triggering events per period.

distinctions.characteristic: Involves loss/absence of a MAJOR limb segment rather than any amputation event
distinctions.why_it_narrows: The raw anchor of all limb amputation/loss events is dominated by minor/partial (digit, partial-foot) amputations that are not fitted with a functional limb prosthesis, so only major-limb events feed this market.

distinctions.characteristic: Recipient is a clinically eligible prosthesis candidate at a qualifying mobility grade
distinctions.why_it_narrows: Many major-limb amputees (frail, dysvascular, diabetic, low-mobility) are never fitted; the German mobility-class (Mobilitätsklasse/K-level) candidacy assessment gates who actually receives a device.

distinctions.characteristic: Device is a reimbursable item listed in the Hilfsmittelverzeichnis under GKV coverage
distinctions.why_it_narrows: Only provision events for devices that clear the German aids-directory listing/coverage gate generate market revenue; events resulting in no reimbursable device supply fall outside the addressable unit.

filters.label: Major-limb-segment filter (exclude minor/digit/partial amputations not fitted with a limb prosthesis)
filters.distinction_ref: Involves loss/absence of a MAJOR limb segment rather than any amputation event

filters.label: Clinical-candidacy / mobility-grade fitment filter (keep only those assessed as prosthesis-eligible at a qualifying Mobilitätsklasse)
filters.distinction_ref: Recipient is a clinically eligible prosthesis candidate at a qualifying mobility grade

filters.label: Reimbursable-listing / GKV-coverage filter (keep only events supplying a Hilfsmittelverzeichnis-listed device)
filters.distinction_ref: Device is a reimbursable item listed in the Hilfsmittelverzeichnis under GKV coverage

price_basis.justification: Revenue accrues per physical prosthesis supplied (and replaced), the discrete reimbursed unit, rather than per procedure or per generic unit.

structure.gap_check: Residual gap on the addition side: a new-amputation event stream undercounts the addressable unit because annual device supply also includes replacement/renewal prostheses for the existing prosthesis-user base (devices wear out on a multi-year cycle and are re-supplied). Filtering amputation events alone never captures these renewal provision events, so the filtered figure is the 'newly fitted' subset, not total devices supplied per year; the replacement-flow component must be added separately. There is also a residual unilateral/bilateral nuance (one event can require more than one device).
structure.double_count_check: The three filters target nominally distinct characteristics — anatomical level (major vs minor), clinical fitment candidacy (mobility grade), and administrative reimbursability (directory listing). Overlap risk: mobility-grade candidacy and reimbursement coverage are partly entangled, since the Mobilitätsklasse assessment is itself a criterion GKV uses to approve funding — so the eligibility filter and the reimbursement filter could remove the same non-funded/non-fitted patients twice. The eligibility filter should be scoped to clinical candidacy and the reimbursement filter to device-listing status to avoid cutting the same population.
